summary:
Occitanie stands under the national legal framework of France. The region-specific record in the sources consists of findings by the CGLPL, the national custodial-inspection authority, at two places of deprivation of liberty in Toulouse.

In its opinion of 25 May 2021, the CGLPL reported on visits to Toulouse-Seysses prison and the Toulouse central police station, concerning eight transgender women held in those facilities. It documented isolation imposed on detainees because of their trans status and staff with no training on trans issues.

The opinion rests on referrals received since 2010 concerning some forty transgender persons, and it finds serious and persisting violations across places of deprivation of liberty. It records that the depathologisation law n° 2016-1547 of 18 November 2016 has never been written into prison rules or healthcare guidance.

The CGLPL recommends financing research, adopting policies against discrimination, and developing suitable procedures for searching and assigning people whose civil-status sex does not match their presented identity. Those procedures govern cell assignment and searches, including strip searches, in the Toulouse facilities it inspected.

No other region-specific incident, enforcement series or divergence record appears in the sources. The absence of a regional record is not evidence of safety in Occitanie's communes.
tangentialFactors:
The BuzzFeed News investigation of January 2018 on trans women in French prisons documents no Occitanie-specific event; the cases it reports arise in Lille and Paris, and the national custody framework it describes applies unchanged in every department, including this one.

The eight transgender women identified in the Toulouse facilities are a raw count with no denominator attached. The sources give no figure for the region's detained population or for the number of trans detainees held in Occitanie at any date, so the count cannot be read as a rate.
localsOnly:
Isolation imposed on detainees because of their trans status was documented inside Toulouse-Seysses prison and the Toulouse central police station, and the CGLPL found staff at those facilities untrained on trans issues.

The depathologisation law n° 2016-1547 of 18 November 2016 has not been written into prison rules or healthcare guidance, so residents subject to those facilities do not receive its protections in practice.

The CGLPL's recommendations are directed at the administration of places of deprivation of liberty: financing research, adopting anti-discrimination policies, and building procedures for searching and assigning people whose civil-status sex does not match their presented identity.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the CGLPL's recommendations of 25 May 2021 have been implemented at Toulouse-Seysses prison or the Toulouse central police station is not sourced, and the current placement of the eight transgender women identified is unresolved.

No comparable findings for detention facilities elsewhere in Occitanie appear in the sources; the region's signal rests on the two Toulouse establishments examined.

No region-specific material on entry screening, document checks or facilities access was identified in the inventory for this region. The national assessment covers those settings.
